description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of large language models, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of SepLLM and StrmLLM, as evaluated in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with linear spacing and major tick marks every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Six distinct lines are plotted: “Vanilla” (purple, solid line) starts near 3.35 and steadily declines to approximately 2.52; “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue, solid) begins near 3.35 and decreases to about 2.65; “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange, solid) starts near 3.3 and drops to roughly 2.55; “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green, solid) begins near 3.25 and converges to about 2.53; “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red, solid) starts near 3.2 and settles around 2.52; and “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue, solid) begins near 3.3 and converges to approximately 2.58. All lines exhibit a steep initial decline in loss followed by a slower, more gradual decrease toward convergence, with the “Vanilla” and “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” models achieving the lowest final loss values.
